**Why this engine:** MCO has erratic accruals, heavy but real SBC, cyclical issuance revenue, and meaningful acquisition amortization. A single normalized P/E or an OCF-less variant hides too much. FCFF from EBIT keeps the leverage structure (78/92 debt-to-value) explicit and lets the cyclical margin recovery show through.

**Cash-flow definition** (per my Section 0 reasoning):
FCFF = EBIT × (1 − 0.21) + D&A − capex − ΔWC
- EBIT is **after SBC** (it is in filed SG&A) — the pack's OCF-SBC warning is satisfied without double-counting.
- D&A add-back is correct because my EBIT is after D&A; capex removes the cash drain.
- ΔWC is modeled but small (+$0.01B/yr) — historical avg ΔWC ≈ +$0.065B/yr across 2015–2025.

**Verdict: DO NOT INITIATE. REDUCE / TRIM EXISTING POSITIONS ON STRENGTH. No margin of safety.**

Moody's is an exceptional franchise — wide-moat duopoly, 46% GAAP operating margins, 53% adjusted margins, F-score 7/8, negative accruals, buybacks, and a Q2 2026 beat of unusual size (adjusted EPS +31%, 15% revenue growth). None of that quality is in dispute. The problem is entirely the price.

At $503, the market is capitalizing a FCF yield of 3.4% and paying 30× forward earnings — which is only justified if one discounts this equity at **≤8.4%** (beta ≈0.85) or assumes high-single-digit growth continues a decade out. My central estimate (β=1.00, WACC 9.0%, terminal growth 4.5%) values the company at ~$426, and my probability-weighted view including the pack's own 1.33 beta is ~$410. The margin of safety at the quoted price is negative on the central case and on the weighted case; only the bull case (which assumes the market's low discount rate is correct) reaches fair value.

**Action:** If you hold MCO, take partial profits into strength above $500; if you do not hold, wait for a pullback toward $410–440 (a 12–18% decline) before initiating. The company itself is a high-quality compounder and belongs on a watchlist for the next issuance downturn; the current price is the wrong entry.
